raw_meta_yaml:
schema_version: 1

context:
  name: py4dgeo
  version: "1.2.1"

package:
  name: ${{ name }}
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  url: https://pypi.org/packages/source/${{ name[0] }}/${{ name }}/${{ name }}-${{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: 21faa7937af5994ee92844db8f39db76b69b007f6db6961e3d3a9f24ae35e101
  patches:
    # option to build against an installed Eigen3 instead of the copy in
    # ext/eigen (to be submitted upstream)
    - patches/0001-Add-PY4DGEO_USE_EXTERNAL_EIGEN-to-use-an-installed-E.patch

build:
  number: 0
  script:
    env:
      # Unix: scikit-build-core otherwise picks "Unix Makefiles", and the CI
      # images have no make. Windows: empty, so the compiler activation picks
      # Visual Studio (it also sets the x64 platform, which Ninja rejects)
      CMAKE_GENERATOR: ${{ "Ninja" if unix else "" }}
    content:
      # bundled Eigen replaced by conda-forge's. The bundled nanoflann (1.9.0,
      # header-only) stays: epoch archives store nanoflann's own KD-tree format,
      # which 2.0 changed (old trees fail to load), and conda-forge has no 1.9;
      # keeping it reads and writes the same archives as the PyPI wheels
      - if: unix
        then: rm -rf ext/eigen ext/benchmark
        else: rmdir /s /q ext\eigen ext\benchmark
      - ${{ PYTHON }} -m pip install . -vv --no-deps --no-build-isolation -Ccmake.define.PY4DGEO_USE_EXTERNAL_EIGEN=ON
  python:
    entry_points:
      - copy_py4dgeo_test_data = py4dgeo.util:copy_test_data_entrypoint

requirements:
  build:
    - ${{ compiler('cxx') }}
    - ${{ stdlib('c') }}
    - cmake >=3.30
    - ninja
    - if: build_platform != target_platform
      then:
        - python
        - cross-python_${{ target_platform }}
        - pybind11
  host:
    - python
    - pip
    - scikit-build-core >=0.11.0
    - pybind11
    - eigen
    # upstream's CMake asks MSVC for /openmp:llvm
    - if: linux
      then: libgomp
      else: llvm-openmp
  run:
    - python
    - dateparser
    - laspy >=2.0,<3.0
    - lazrs-python
    - matplotlib-base
    - numpy
    - pandas
    - pooch
    - psutil
    - requests
    - scikit-learn
    - scipy
    - seaborn-base
    - xdg

tests:
  - python:
      imports:
        - py4dgeo
      pip_check: true
  # upstream's tests download their data from Zenodo; this one has a known answer
  - script:
      - python test_m3c2.py
    files:
      recipe:
        - test_m3c2.py
        - epoch_pypi_1.2.1.zip

about:
  homepage: https://github.com/3dgeo-heidelberg/py4dgeo
  repository: https://github.com/3dgeo-heidelberg/py4dgeo
  documentation: https://py4dgeo.readthedocs.io
  summary: Library for change detection in 4D point cloud data
  description: |
    py4dgeo implements change analysis in multi-temporal point clouds:
    M3C2 (with level of detection) and its variants, cloud-to-cloud distances,
    registration and spatiotemporal segmentation, with a C++ core.
  license: MIT
  license_file:
    - LICENSE.md
    - ext/nanoflann/COPYING

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - Tobias-Fischer
